facts.fact: An attachment between two people is objectively real, arrives involuntarily, is mutual, and is observable by third parties. Proximity intensifies it.
An attachment confers no combat power, no telepathy, and no ability to read another person's intent, and entitles neither party to anything.

The binding vow has two halves. Both must be spoken freely and knowingly before an accepted witness, separated by an interval — it is designed to be spoken in two parts so consent is deliberate. It cannot be completed accidentally, in sleep, under compulsion, by proxy, or in the same breath.
Speaking one half of the vow binds only the speaker, stripping that person's protections and leaving the other party entirely free.

Elias Marrow spoke the first half of the binding vow to June Havlik in the Grant Street deposition suite, before Father Bram Delisle as accepted witness, interrupting the reading of clause one. It is recorded in the deposition transcript June later certified.
An exposed trustee can be compelled, sued, and claimed by any party with standing, until the vow is answered or formally abandoned.

Before completion, the speaker may formally abandon a spoken half. Abandonment ends that half-vow and the speaker's exposure but does not sever the involuntary attachment. Its permanent price is excommunication: removal from every lineage office, succession, institutional protection, and enforcement standing, while ordinary civil identity and individually held civil property remain. Once a bond has completed, no abandonment, annulment, or severance exists.
facts.origin: Author decision, 2026-08-21; abandonment existence established in B1E02 and its permanent price disclosed in repaired B1E05

facts.fact: Direct sunlight destroys a trustee. There is no exception, no tolerance acquired with age, and no exemption granted as a reward.
Trustees may be awake and abroad during daytime hours provided they remain out of direct sunlight. Daylight legal business is conducted by human attorneys of record.
Members change on the three nights bracketing the full moon, involuntarily, on a publicly available calendar. There is no exemption and no suppressant that works.
A trustee cannot enter a dwelling without an invitation from someone who lives there, and that invitation is revocable at any time by the person who gave it.

facts.fact: A supernatural obligation exists only once it is named aloud before witnesses, and is discharged only by performance of what was named. This governs lineage-enforceable obligations only.

Cutting severs an incomplete attachment. It is permanent and survivable: the person cut remembers loving and cannot feel it. A completed bond cannot be cut, because it exists in both registers and in a living witness's memory, and no instrument reaches it.
Vera Odell is a cutter. Her price is always a deed, never money, and she quotes it in full before touching anything and honors it exactly.
Attachments are recorded in both lineages' registers, so a severance leaves a documentary hole that someone must account for.
Local Nine has registered two attachments in nineteen years. Registrations are declining measurably each decade across both lineages.
June formally declined to have her attachment cut, on the record. Declining is itself a documented election, noted in both registers.
Local Nine has 311 members in good standing. Its charter is contingent on the Articles being honored.
Neither June nor her mother appears on Local Nine's roster. Her mother's line was closed with a date and a notation when she left the Hall.
Marta Havlik personally signed the notation closing June's mother's roster line, and refuses to say why her sister left.
June was never initiated into Local Nine and therefore has no membership, vote, benefits, or standing to renounce. Wolf law does not recognize an uninitiated person of wolf blood.

Local Nine's roster contains a gap that Yolanda Bright has maintained for nineteen years. The gap and a later alteration to the Hall minutes were made by the same person for the same reason, and that person is not Yolanda.

facts.fact: Before completion, refusal is absolute: either party may withhold their half of the vow indefinitely, for any reason or none, and no pressure, symptom, clause, or debt can supply it for them.
A completed bond can never be dissolved by any means. Neither register holds an instrument of erasure — only annotation.

Exactly five facts become permanent on completion: each always knows the other's direction and rough distance; each knows when the other is dying; the mortal party stops aging and remains entirely killable; neither can ever form or complete another attachment; and both are permanently recorded as bonded in both registers, conferring standing that cannot be struck.

A completed bond guarantees no love, obedience, fidelity, compatibility, allegiance, proximity, or happiness, and grants no telepathy, shared emotion, or compulsion. Bonded people may separate, betray each other, or become enemies.

Completion permanently forfeits both parties' capacity to swear any other binding oath, because no one may stand in two conflicting records. A bonded trustee can never hold an office requiring an oath; a bonded member can never be initiated.

No supernatural obligation takes hold until it enters a record, and the two lineages disagree in good faith about what a record is: trustees are bound by writing, members by what is borne and witnessed. This governs lineage-enforceable obligation only. Ordinary promises, debts, crimes, affection, and human legal duties are fully binding without any record, and a refusal is absolute without one.

Cutters price their work in deeds rather than money because a cut is a crime against a record and no institution in either system will enforce a cutter's fee; a deed performed in view is their only security. This is a feature of that trade, not a universal law — both lineages transact in money and property routinely.
Members smell fear, arousal, illness, recent violence, and blood kinship. Sustained face-to-face lying is effectively impossible among them, and no filing can alter what a body records.

facts.fact: Trustees cannot smell a lie and believe nothing that is not written, sealed, and filed. Kinship among them is appointment, not blood, and a successor is named by instrument.
A trustee reads 'bride' as a position to be filled; a member hears a body being taken out of a line. Neither can be argued out of their reading.
Members punish by exile, which is removal from presence. Trustees punish by excommunication, which is removal from the record.
Because a completed bond cannot be cut, it lies beyond the reach of the severance market. This is why a completed bond is worth a war, and why the Marrow Trust needs one to survive the century.

Consent is never subject to the record principle. A record is required to create a supernatural obligation, never to validate a refusal: an unrecorded refusal is absolute and immediate, silence is a refusal, and withdrawal requires no formality.
June's clarification for the record in B1E01 is what compelled the accepted witness to state aloud that the half-spoken vow bound only the speaker. Her professional instinct produced the disclosure.
June certified the transcript of her own naming and of the vow that followed it, making her a participant in the record that binds him.
The next full moon after June's naming is nineteen days out. She has no safe room, no housing slot, and no benefit coverage, because none of that exists for someone off the roster.
June served a written demand for the certified copy of the Articles, witnessed and spoken aloud — using both record systems at once before she understood that was what she was doing.
The Sewickley house verifies its own records by one steward reading aloud while another listens, checking a written record against a borne one.
One of the seven named brides is alive and unaccounted for by the Trust. The stewards' ledger holds a forwarding address for her that nobody has requested in ninety years.
The released bride survived not by fighting the Articles but by making herself indispensable to a third party with standing.

June has been reading the borne record unconsciously her entire career and calling it instinct. From B1E13 she begins doing it deliberately. This is a literacy she already possessed, not a power the bond granted.
June bought a safe-room slot from a member with her own rent money, then returned it when he needed it back, leaving herself unhoused for the moon.
